arguments.value: David Alan Ezra, born in 1947 in Columbus, Ohio, is a United States district judge for the District of Hawaii. He earned a B.B.A. from St. Mary’s University in 1969 and a J.D. from St. Mary’s University School of Law in 1972. After serving in the U.S. Army Reserve from 1971 to 1977, he worked as a law clerk in the Office of the Corporation Counsel for the City and County of Honolulu in 1972 and then entered private practice in Honolulu, where he practiced from 1972 to 1988. He has served as an adjunct professor of law at the William S. Richardson School of Law since 1978, was appointed to the federal bench in 1988, served as chief judge from 1999 to 2005, and assumed senior status in 2012.
